title: Why Google returns different results to different users
why: Locale and context-dependent results are intended for relevance at scale; the critique misunderstands how search is designed.

title: Why prosecuting individual bankers misses systemic causes
why: The crisis stemmed from system structure rather than individual crimes, so prosecution alone cannot explain or prevent it.

title: Butler's critique of war profits and WWII reverence
why: Argues war profits and manufacturers' interests drive conflicts; mostly political opinion about WWI and WWII.

title: Speculation on interstellar hitchhiking and black hole power
why: Speculative futurism about asteroids, stellar wanderers and black hole propulsion without a grounded mechanism.

title: Cultural swings from back-to-nature to the alt-right
why: Sweeping interpretive essay on 1970s movements and broadcast TV; opinion without verifiable substance.

title: Crichton quote on mass media and cultural diversity
why: Quoted fiction argues mass media homogenizes culture; a rhetorical opinion rather than evidence.

title: Critique of a laptop review's processor comparisons
why: Argues clock speed alone is a poor CPU comparison, but mostly a complaint about one laptop and its buyers.

title: Judging startup finalists by market competitiveness
why: Opinionated critique of finalists based on crowded markets, narrow ceilings and problems customers do not care about.

title: Ending federal student loans to discipline tuition
why: Policy argument that dischargeable private lending would curb college fees; contested opinion rather than evidence.

title: Google vs Facebook engineering culture differences
why: Facebook ships fast with incremental tweaks while Google funds long-shot projects; also a developer, engineer and computer scientist taxonomy.

title: Tesla camera coverage against legal driving vision standards
why: Converts 20/40 acuity into pixels per degree and compares Tesla camera fields and ranges, treating each camera as a single eye.

title: Why musical instruments outlast computers
why: Analogy comparing synthesizers with laptops and a wish for durable computing; no technical explanation.

title: Facebook's harms as emergent system properties
why: Persuasive argument that bad outcomes emerged from a system built for good purposes; opinion without data.

title: Weighing the four COVID origin theories
why: Plausibility reasoning about origin hypotheses that depends on trust in governments; opinion rather than analysis.

title: Why incumbents beat newcomers on hardware cost
why: Vertical integration gives Samsung and Apple cost edges, so startups need a niche edge; mostly startup advice.

title: Anecdote about dietary cholesterol narratives
why: Personal story and distrust of public health messaging; quotes a study abstract but offers no analysis.

title: Carrier control versus iOS control of devices
why: Motivational argument that carriers and manufacturers control Android; opinion on platform openness.

title: Mosquitoes cause far more human deaths than other animals
why: Ranks animals by annual human deaths, putting mosquitoes near one million, well ahead of humans, snakes and dogs.

title: Why agrarian economies stay labor-heavy and high-fertility
why: Below about 1 MWh per capita a country lacks steel and nitrogen fertilizer, so farming stays labor-intensive and families grow large.

title: Arbitrary notation and how math should be taught
why: Opinion that mathematical symbols are arbitrary and should be taught as exploration; no concrete evidence offered.

title: Ergonomics spending priorities for a desk setup
why: Spend heavily on an adjustable chair and quality keyboard since they last years; try midrange chairs before buying premium.

title: Argument over unsafe code in Rust crates
why: Back-and-forth reply about unsafe matrices and optimizer tradeoffs; only makes sense within the thread.

title: Evolved programs exploited timing side channels in fitness functions
why: Classifiers evolved timing loops to exploit database latency, and agents coordinated via scheduler timing; fitness functions get gamed.

title: Trivia-style interviews versus real engineering work
why: Opinion that algorithm trivia interviews select for the wrong skills; argues for paid trial work instead.

title: Why companies avoid hiring junior developers
why: Economic argument that training costs and salary jumps make newcomers unattractive; plausible but opinion-driven.

title: Chennai's groundwater dependence and broken water pipes
why: Borewells hide the shortage for now, but the pipe network leaks, lacks metering and rarely delivers beyond drinking water.

title: Asian American admissions disadvantage argument
why: Political argument about race-based admissions and quotas; contested opinion rather than teachable analysis.

title: Whether everyone should learn programming
why: Opinion essay arguing programming is applied logical thinking; persuasive but not technical knowledge.

title: Shkreli's alleged harassment and bragging interview
why: News-level commentary on an arrest and an interview; no technical or educational lesson.

title: Whether using a donated Starbucks card was theft
why: Moral debate about a card experiment; opinion on ethics with no transferable technical content.

title: Whether girlish preferences are shameful
why: Personal argument about gender norms and princess marketing; opinion rather than substantive insight.

title: Subsidizing demand while supply stays flat
why: Policy argument that education subsidies raised prices without adding capacity; contested opinion on taxpayer spending.

title: Why Tesla is targeted by labor organizers
why: Speculative argument about union motives and interest groups; opinionated and not verifiable here.

title: Why the default DoH resolver choice matters
why: ISPs routinely monitor plaintext DNS, and a default resolver must handle huge load and be on the HSTS preload list.

title: Tesla's Q3 discounts boosted quarterly profit
why: Insider-flavored account of discounting to hit numbers; interesting context but no transferable lesson.

title: Plant communication and vegan ethics
why: Argues plants signal and respond to stress, framed as a rebuttal to vegans; mostly opinion with unsourced claims.

title: The Seattle Freeze and local versus transplant divides
why: Personal social observations about Seattle; anecdotal experience with no broader lesson.

title: A self-taught programmer's path into Cambridge research
why: Personal account of feeling unprepared among famous researchers; name-dropping and anecdote rather than teachable method.

title: Reading a meta-analysis skeptically: outcomes, multiplicity, certainty
why: Most outcomes were null and the one positive result rests on two studies without multiple-comparison adjustment, so certainty is fragile.

title: Exceptions should not signal expected missing records
why: Design opinion that routine conditions like missing records should return values; useful taste but not substantive explanation.

title: Four compounding causes of San Francisco's housing shortage
why: 1970s court rulings, Petaluma-style growth caps, and Prop 13 with rent control froze supply and pushed prices up.

title: Critique of a candidate's emails and job search
why: Blunt personal critique of a job seeker's writing style; advice-flavored opinion without technical substance.

title: Teaching data structures in Python instead of Java
why: Dropping Java generics and access modifiers let the course focus on algorithms, complexity and hand-compiling to MIPS.

title: Refusing unethical bulk data requests from buyers
why: Anecdote about refusing customers' surveillance requests and offering research data at cost; ethics story, no lesson.

title: Testing Whisper on French speech and translation
why: On an RTX 3090 a 6-minute French video translated in about 22 seconds; transcription was good but made notable errors.

title: Practical security advice beyond validating input
why: Dry-run platform updates, build servers from known source, and track dependency fixes, since input validation alone buys little.

title: Apple A13 single-core speed rivals top desktop chips
why: Geekbench shows a phone-class chip matching top x86 single-core scores, hinting Apple's design could beat x86 in desktops, though phones cannot sustain bursts.

title: Why US hardware startups struggle with regulation and liability
why: Patent minefields, medical regulation, liability and labor costs make manufacturing painful, pushing many founders toward software.

title: How Reddit's subreddit ad targeting changed for visitors
why: Recent visitors to a subreddit or its posts now qualify for subreddit-targeted ads, not only subscribers, as the help docs describe.

title: Why recommendations should surprise rather than repeat
why: Opinion that engines should suggest what users do not yet know they want; reasonable taste, but not substantive.

title: Nextdoor's racism and weak neighborhood verification
why: Anecdote about discriminatory posts plus a claim that billing address verification is weak; mostly opinion and complaint.

title: Practical gotchas for entrepreneurs moving to Canada
why: Immigration services profit from newcomers; apply for OHIP immediately on arrival, and expect to build credit history from scratch.

title: Why Linux driver and GUI API complaints miss the point
why: Most drivers already ship in the kernel; the real gap is GUI toolkits that break compatibility, unlike Win32's decades of binary stability.

title: Why facial expressions cannot reliably reveal emotions
why: Emotion expression involves the whole body, unfolds over time, overlaps heavily and is culturally learned and masked, so recognition is context-dependent.

title: Praise for Svelte's documentation and simplicity
why: Enthusiastic framework comparison and rant about React churn; opinion rather than a technical explanation.

title: How Amazon's written and verbal performance management diverge
why: Written rules stress objective evaluation, but unspoken attrition targets push managers to place lowest performers on improvement plans.

title: Why air combat technology still matters more than rifles
why: Argument about fighter jets versus rifles and a critic's views; opinionated defense debate rather than teachable analysis.

title: Objections to on-device CSAM scanning
why: Policy and privacy argument about device scanning and trust; opinion on ownership rather than technical explanation.

title: How HFT quants differ from other finance engineers
why: Quant traders earn a share of profits and need trading psychology; non-trading engineers earn salaries, and HFT is modern arbitrage.

title: Parenting causes of childhood ADHD diagnoses
why: Anecdotal trend claims about parents and medication with no data; opinion presented as observation.

title: Why signed overflow undefined behavior enables loop optimization
why: Compilers assume i+16 never overflows, allowing unrolling and precomputation; defined wrapping would block those optimizations in hot loops.

title: Why visual tools hide complexity that programmers need
why: Opinion that tools hiding implementation details frustrate experienced programmers; a reasonable view but not substantive.

title: Why apps are almost certainly not secretly listening
why: Speech recognition would drain CPU or bandwidth, iOS shows mic use, and researchers reverse-engineer traffic; apparent eavesdropping is coincidence at scale.

title: Ok and Cancel button placement debate
why: Designer's opinion that placement should be internally consistent, with arguments for each side; no hard technical content.

title: Glare explanation for the Navy UFO video
why: Speculation about UFOs, religion and conspiracy psychology; opinion rather than verified technical analysis.

title: Google wage equity and gender debate
why: Contested opinion on gender bias and hiring preferences; political argument rather than teachable insight.

title: Benchmarking ripgrep against GNU grep on the Linux kernel
why: With equal parallelism ripgrep is about 2x faster; the 10x gain comes from default filters that search less data, not raw speed.

title: Three moderation strategies and Section 230 tradeoffs
why: Framework of no moderation, pre-vetting, and post-hoc moderation is useful, but the piece is a policy argument about regulation.

title: Polished how-to videos often carry less accurate advice
why: Experienced tradespeople's shaky jobsite videos often hold the best tricks; production polish signals video skill, not craft expertise.

title: Personal struggles with sleep and focus
why: Personal anecdote about sleep schedules and blue light; no transferable explanation or source.

title: Why package delays differ from flats mail capacity
why: Flats sorting machines cannot process packages, so cutting them and overtime slows parcels without necessarily hurting ballot-scale flats.

title: Solve others' problems rather than create a startup
why: Generic founder advice: focus on others' needs, limit the scope and work alone; motivational rather than specific.

title: Why 21700 cells trade power density for energy
why: 21700 cells deliver less power per weight than 18650s, so Tesla's performance cars would need throttling or heavier battery packs.

title: What the 8-foot police filming rule actually means
why: Parties to an interaction may film closer; non-party bystanders can be asked to stay 8 feet back, a distance courts already upheld.

title: Lifestyle notes on remote consulting in the UK
why: Personal lifestyle comparison of cities and currency effects; relevant to the author only.

title: Romantic love as a delusion and lookism
why: Provocative opinion on attraction and marriage; contested views rather than teachable knowledge.

title: Starship delays and launch economics
why: Prediction and opinion about Starship and SLS costs; informed-sounding but speculative.

title: Why Intel Macs throttle when driving external displays
why: Driving monitors pushed Intel Macs onto the discrete GPU, adding heat that the thin chassis could not dissipate.

title: Why scope-based defer breaks when cleanup moves to helpers
why: Deferred cleanup runs when the creating function returns, so helpers hand back closed resources; value-based destructors avoid this.

title: Diversity debates as a cultural pendulum
why: Personal grievance about diversity circles framed as a pendulum; opinion and political argument.

title: Brazilian protests and corruption perspective
why: Political account from a citizen abroad; opinion on government and taxes rather than technical insight.

title: Why bright indoor light needs daytime cues and dimming limits
why: Clocks handle photoperiods only up to about 14-15 hours; long bright indoor days shift rhythms, so automatic dimming after late hours matters.

title: Critique of an article on WWI parallels
why: Rebuttal of historical analogies with some points on Ottoman decline and alliances; argumentative rather than explanatory.

title: How fiber taps evade OTDR detection by avoiding cuts
why: A 99/1 beam splitter diverts a sliver of photons without breaking the fiber, so operators' OTDR fault tests never reveal a break.

title: Frustrating Gmail verification flow and a workaround
why: Complaint about a login flow and an incognito workaround; personal experience with minimal general lesson.

title: A social feed limited to 25 friends
why: Product idea for a capped social feed; opinion and speculation rather than evidence.

title: Cold batteries and reduced regenerative braking
why: Driver experience of regen degrading in cold batteries; anecdotal, though it hints at battery temperature effects.

title: Small talk and social skills versus reading
why: Opinion that social skills matter more than reading books; advice without substantive evidence.

title: HN moderation downweighting and community flags
why: Moderator note about how comments are downweighted and why; a moderation notice, not technical content.

title: Skepticism that the singularity is a realistic path
why: Opinion that singularity thinking is a cargo cult; contested view without supporting analysis.

title: Degrees versus actual job requirements in tech support
why: Personal anecdote about a company hiring degree-holders for basic troubleshooting; no transferable mechanism.

title: Why global ranked ladders are poor game design
why: Designer's opinion that cheating and incentives make global ladders hard to justify; reasoned but judgment-based.

title: Why lenses cannot ignite fires from moonlight
why: Lenses cannot concentrate light beyond its source brightness, and moonlight is dilute reflected sunlight, not a hot emitter.

title: Defending comments that explain obvious code
why: Opinion that explanatory comments aid readers and create narrative; a style preference rather than new knowledge.

title: How a kernel driver update caused boot loops
why: A faulty sensor pushed to production crashed Windows; recovery meant attaching each cloud disk to a working node and deleting the driver file.

title: Craig Murray on the Assange prosecution
why: Quoted political commentary on Swedish charges and bail; news and opinion, not technical knowledge.

title: Desktop OS should abstract files via assistants
why: Wishful opinion that file management should be replaced by AI assistants; a vision, not an explanation.

title: Confusing electrode labels in tDCS brain stimulation papers
why: Studies label contacts active and reference instead of anode and cathode, and left-right placement depends on perspective, complicating replication.

title: Personal experience of disability denial and poverty
why: Moving personal account of denied benefits and a comparison with Europe; experience-based opinion, no mechanism explained.

title: Why solar roads make no economic sense
why: Argues solar roads lose efficiency and cost more to build and maintain; reasoned critique but largely opinion with rough estimates.
